title: Nothing to Be Ashamed Of
author: The Daily Dad
summary: This Daily Dad reflection uses a scene from Theodore Roosevelt's presidential inauguration to make a point about fatherly affection. Drawing on Doris Kearns Goodwin's The Bully Pulpit, it notes that on one of the proudest days of his life Roosevelt was not playing it cool but scanning the crowd for his wife and children. When he found them he waved openly, not furtively or half-heartedly, but with demonstration frank and full. The piece turns this into a standard for fathers: family should light us up, and that delight should be shown rather than suppressed. It quietly challenges the assumption that masculine composure requires hiding domestic love.
points: Roosevelt, at the height of his public triumph, was most focused on finding his young family in the inauguration crowd.
Goodwin's account describes his wave as frank and full, not the embarrassed gesture of a man hiding domestic affection.
The piece rejects the idea that a man should tamp down visible enthusiasm for his wife and children.
Fathers are urged to let their family light them up and to show that love proudly, especially after time apart.
quotes: It was one of the proudest days of his life. He had come so far. He had won, been elected by the people, had conquered his early childhood weaknesses, had become, as he would later say, the man in the arena.

So on the day of his presidential inauguration, you might think that Theodore Roosevelt was feeling pretty powerful. Or you might think, as a man, he was trying to keep his enthusiasm under wraps, trying to play the whole thing off, act cool.
In fact, what he was thinking about was his wife and kids, who were the most important people in the world to him.
Roosevelt scanned the crowd for his young family, and when he saw them, he lit up.
Waving not “furtively nor half-heartedly, nor as if he were afraid someone might see this evidence of his domestic affection, but with demonstration frank and full.
And that’s how we should feel when we see our family (especially if we’ve been parted from each other). They should light us up.
We should not be afraid to show it, should not tamp it down. We should embrace that love and enthusiasm we naturally feel for them, and show it proudly.
